Q8_reason: I find it hard to tell how many meters it is, but counting steps is way easier since it’s tied to my actual body movements, making it easier to react. Being aware of the situation just gives me a better sense of security, so I’m less likely to get hit.

- In Steps mode, it speaks more when it needs to and speaks less when it does not need to. For example, when the object is far away it speaks less, because I roughly know the number of steps, so less speaking is fine. When I get close it counts down like 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, so I clearly knows when to stop. This countdown feels comfortable. In Metres mode, I don't know when it will start announcing, which feels unsafe.
- When decelerating I can know exactly when to stop.
- In Metres mode I don't know how far it actually is and has to calculate it myself. Steps are easier to quantify. Walking while mentally calculating how much distance is left is tiring and troublesome.

I didn't know how far 3 metres actually was, and I was afraid of bumping into things, so I had to stop every time I heard an announcement and wait for the next one to confirm before I could take another step. But with steps, I could count how many steps I had taken and how many were left, and the remaining steps the system announced roughly matched what I was counting in my head, so I trusted it more.

In steps mode, when I was getting close there was a countdown, and it announced once for every step I took, so I could react immediately and decide whether to stop. But in metres mode there was nothing like that. I had to rely almost entirely on instinct to judge how close I was to the obstacle, and I kept wondering whether the remaining one metre meant the distance before I took a step or after, which made me feel unsafe.

With steps I could roughly picture where the obstacle was in my head. It felt more intuitive compared to metres, since I am not very sensitive to numbers. And the decimal part in metres was really hard to understand in terms of how far that actually was.
